items.title: George Guesnon Interview
items.q: I went to him and I took lessons with him for about seven months. And when he turned me loose, he said, There ain't anything no more I can show you.

ctx.x: Well, no. You see, that's where I was better than he was. You see, that's what made me, as I say, I'm better than my teacher. As far as that goes. You see, my banjo playing today, that's what makes me stand out as a banjo player. It isn't that I make more chords than the other fella, or I read more better than him. I can solo more better than him. You see, I take all single-string solos. We'll say like Charlie Christian or somebody like that. And you get the beauty about taking all them broken-off pegs of yours…
Anything else about John Marrero's style? What kind of a banjo did he use?
Well, he used the standard vega them days. You see, the vega was...
